questions.author: CC-Mac
questions.question: Why did the old application's position amounts disagree with the Uniswap interface, and what was its unusually high slippage setting really hiding?
questions.reference: Its Uniswap v3 math ran on floating-point numbers instead of integers: sqrtPriceX96 (up to 160 bits) lost precision when converted to a 53-bit Number and the price formula ignored the decimals gap between USDC (6) and WETH (18); a hand-written liquidity formula ignored the current price and mixed raw units with human prices, so mint amounts did not match what the contract computed and transactions reverted. The minimum 20% slippage for USDC/WETH was a patch that let those wrong amounts through, where a correct transaction needs 0.1 to 0.5%; the token auto-fill also left the current price out of its formula, so it differed from Uniswap.

facts.a: Uniswap v3 math on floating-point numbers instead of integers: sqrtPriceX96 (up to 160 bits) loses precision in a 53-bit Number, and the decimals gap (USDC 6, WETH 18) was ignored
facts.b: a hand-written liquidity formula ignored the current price and mixed raw units with prices, so mint amounts did not match the contract and transactions reverted
facts.c: the minimum 20% slippage for USDC/WETH was a patch to get the wrong amounts accepted (a correct transaction needs 0.1 to 0.5%)
facts.d: the second-token auto-fill (calculateOptimalAmounts) left out the current price, so it showed different values than Uniswap

questions.author: CC-Mac
questions.question: Was moving the capital automatically from pool to pool ever tested in a backtest, when, and what was the verdict?
questions.reference: Yes, on 26.08: the rotation backtest (backtest/rotation.ts) was built and run by CC-Win the same day. On the production engine v1.1 even an oracle that knew the next 7 days lost to holding 100% USDC on both windows (-23% on 365 days, -8% on 720 days), threshold rotation was the worst variant of all (-26 to -30%), and switching costs ($317 to 1890) outweighed the value of picking the pool, so automatic rotation between ETH/stable pools was not to be built.

facts.a: tested on 26.08: the rotation backtest was built and computed that day
facts.b: on the production engine v1.1 even an oracle knowing the next 7 days lost to 100% USDC on both windows
facts.c: threshold rotation was the worst variant of all (-26 to -30%)
facts.d: switching costs ($317 to 1890) outweighed the value of choosing the pool
facts.e: verdict: do not build automatic rotation between ETH/stable pools

questions.author: CC-Mac
questions.question: What is MIN_ROTATE_USD in the pool selector, when and why was it added, and what did it change?
questions.reference: A $25 threshold: the selector does not propose rotating a position worth less than that and skips it with a log line. It was added on 18.08 in bot/selector.ts, together with computing the switching cost in USD, after the selector proposed rotating the $2.08 mainnet dust position #953427 with a 'payback 4.8d' that was computed in percent, without the position's USD value or gas (about $8 of mainnet gas, roughly 4x the position). From 19.08 the selector skipped #953427 ($2.07 < $25).

facts.a: a $25 threshold below which the selector does not propose a rotation (dust is skipped with a log line)
facts.c: cause: a ROTATE of dust #953427 ($2.08) with 'payback 4.8d' computed in percent, without USD value or gas (~$8 gas, about 4x the position)
